question: In parasitology, what exactly are parasitic ova?

options.A: The egg stage of parasitic worms
options.B: The larval stage found in blood
options.C: The spore of an opportunistic fungus
options.D: The adult form of a protozoan

explanation: Think of ova simply as the eggs laid by parasitic worms (helminths) so they can reproduce and spread to new hosts! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h1)

question: Why do female parasitic worms lay thousands of eggs (ova) every single day?

options.A: To repair damaged intestinal mucosal linings
options.B: To strengthen the immune system of the host
options.C: To guarantee species survival and transmission
options.D: To provide extra nutrients for the host body

explanation: Since the journey to a new host is tough and full of hazards, laying massive numbers of eggs ensures that at least some survive to keep the species going. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h1)

question: Which tough outer layer protects parasitic eggs from harsh outside conditions?
explanation: The chitin shell acts like a tiny, sturdy armor, protecting the developing embryo from harsh environments until it finds a host. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is the main job of an operculum found on certain parasite eggs?

options.A: It anchors the egg securely to bowel walls
options.B: It prevents staining during microscopy preparation
options.C: It acts as a hatch-lid for larval exit
options.D: It triggers an immediate allergic response

explanation: An operculum is like a tiny trapdoor or hatch-lid that pops open when the time is right, letting the baby larva swim out! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h2)

question: Which group of parasite eggs is famous for having a bumpy, rough outer coat (called a mammillated coat)?
explanation: Nematode eggs, like those of Ascaris lumbricoides, often feature a bumpy, rough outer layer that helps identify them under the microscope. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h3)

question: What special feature makes Schistosoma eggs stand out from other parasite eggs?

options.C: A spiral band of cilia outside

explanation: Schistosoma eggs are easily recognized by a sharp spine (either on the side or at the tip) which helps them pierce through tissues. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h3)

question: How do most intestinal parasitic eggs commonly spread to new people?
explanation: The faeco-oral route is the main culprit—usually happening when food, water, or hands become contaminated with tiny, invisible traces of infected waste. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why do some parasitic eggs need to pass through an intermediate host (like a snail) before they can infect humans?

options.A: To undergo necessary developmental stages before infecting humans
options.B: To allow the adult worms to reproduce inside aquatic animals
options.C: To increase the total physical size of the egg capsule
options.D: To protect the eggs from being destroyed by human stomach acid

explanation: Some parasites need a pit stop in an animal like a snail to transform into the exact form that can successfully infect a human. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h4)

question: What common health problem develops in a patient carrying a heavy load of intestinal worms over a long period?
explanation: Intestinal worms steal vital nutrients and blood from the host, frequently leading to poor growth, weakness, and anemia. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h5)

question: How do Schistosoma eggs cause damage to organs like the liver or bladder inside an infected person?

options.A: By triggering granulomatous inflammation in organs
options.B: By releasing large amounts of digestive enzymes
options.C: By blocking nerve impulses along the spinal cord
options.D: By directly consuming red blood cells in veins

explanation: When the eggs get trapped in body tissues, the body's immune system reacts by forming clusters of cells (granulomas) that cause local damage. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h5)

question: What is the primary specimen collected in the hospital to diagnose intestinal parasite eggs?
explanation: Since these parasites live in the gut, a fresh stool sample is the standard specimen sent to the lab for microscopic checks. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h6)

question: Why do laboratory scientists use concentration methods when examining stool samples for parasite eggs?

options.A: To dissolve the outer chitin shell for better staining
options.B: To separate bacteria from the parasite eggs easily
options.C: To find eggs when numbers in the sample are low
options.D: To kill any live larvae present before laboratory handling

explanation: Concentrating the sample gets rid of heavy debris and gathers the eggs together, making them much easier to spot under the microscope. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h6)

question: What public health term describes treating an entire community at risk with deworming medications at once?
explanation: Mass drug administration (MDA) is a strategy where entire communities in high-risk areas receive deworming tablets to quickly lower infection rates. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h7)

question: As a nurse, which simple preventive action directly stops the faeco-oral spread of intestinal parasite eggs?

options.A: Isolating infected patients in private hospital rooms
options.B: Screening all hospital staff for adult worm infections
options.C: Promoting handwashing and safe excreta disposal

explanation: Good hygiene habits like proper handwashing and safe waste disposal break the cycle, keeping eggs away from our food and water! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h7)
